approachQuestion.prompt: Two lowercase strings a and b contain excerpts. Return the length of their longest identical contiguous fragment, or zero if they share no character. Examples: a="abxc", b="abc" → 2; a="zz", b="yy" → 0; a="aba", b="bab" → 2. Which approach is most suitable?
constraints: 1 ≤ m=a.length,n=b.length ≤ 1500. Strings are read-only; return a length only.

options.text: Keep two zero-initialized rows of n+1 lengths and a global maximum. At prefix pair (i,j), set the current value to previous[j−1]+1 on equal last characters and zero otherwise. Update the maximum, reset column zero each row, and swap row references.
options.feedback: The cell measures a common fragment ending at those exact positions. A mismatch breaks contiguity and forces zero; the answer may end at any prefix pair.

options.text: Use the same common-ending-fragment recurrence but retain the full prefix-pair table.
options.feedback: This computes the correct result on the whole domain, but retains old states that future transitions never read. Removing those states preserves correctness and reduces auxiliary storage.

options.text: On a mismatch take the maximum of above and left, as for a common subsequence.
options.feedback: For a="abxc", b="abc", this returns 3 for nonadjacent abc, whereas the longest common fragment has length 2.

options.text: Return only the cell for the full lengths after the matching-or-zero recurrence.
options.feedback: For a="abx", b="aby", the final cell is zero but the earlier fragment ab has length 2.

feedback.reason: Use a common-ending state with mismatch reset and a global maximum to enforce contiguity.
details: Allocate two rows of n+1 lengths. Compute all m×n common-ending cells, updating a scalar maximum. Swap references without copying, keeping b as the column dimension.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Allocate two rows of n+1 lengths. Compute all m×n common-ending cells, updating a scalar maximum. Swap references without copying, keeping b as the column dimension. Analyze this fixed implementation. N=m+n; m,n vary independently. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Array indexing and word arithmetic take constant time. No hashing, amortized containers, recursion, slicing, or input copying is used. Count all allocated work arrays and temporaries; exclude the read-only input and scalar output.
Include initialization; treat the stated dimensions as variable parameters within their bounds. Use a word per stored counter or flag, not a packed bitset.

feedback.reason: Compute all m*n ending pairs using two n+1 rows and one maximum.
details: Each cell uses a constant-time character comparison and update. Only two n+1-entry rows and a scalar maximum survive; no fragments are copied or reconstructed.
“O(m+n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The method computes all mn prefix pairs, not a single aligned pass.
“O(mn) time, O(mn) auxiliary space”: The fixed method retains only two rows and the global maximum.
“O(mn) time, O(min(m,n)) auxiliary space”: Rows always use b.length+1 entries. The fixed algorithm does not exchange the strings.
